turns.t: Hi. My eyes feel, I don't know, dry and gritty. Mostly when I'm on my computer.
How long has that been happening?
Months, probably. It's been getting worse. By the end of the day they're burning, and I'm squinting.
Does it affect both eyes? ~
Both. Sometimes they water a lot, which is weird, because they feel dry. ~
That's actually very common, the eye waters because it's irritated. How many hours a day are you on screens? ~
Eight or nine at work, and then I'm on my phone in the evening. ~
When you look at a screen, do you notice how often you blink? ~
I never thought about it. Probably not much. ~
Most people blink about half as often when they concentrate on a screen. ~
Really? So that's why. ~
It's a big part of it. Your tear film dries out between blinks. ~
Is it serious? ~
Not at all. It's called digital eye strain with dry eye, and it's very treatable without any tests. ~
Do I need glasses? ~
When did you last have your eyes tested? ~
Er, maybe three years ago. ~
Book a check-up at your optician, because uncorrected vision makes eye strain worse. ~
I'll do that. ~
In the meantime, follow the twenty-twenty-twenty rule: every twenty minutes, look at something twenty feet away for twenty seconds.
I've heard of that one. ~
And blink deliberately, fully, a few times each minute, particularly when you're reading. ~
Right. ~
Make sure your screen is slightly below eye level, and about an arm's length away.
Mine's above my head, practically. ~
Then lower it. And if your office has air conditioning blowing at your face, move away from it. ~
Good point, it's right above me. ~
A warm compress on your closed eyes for a few minutes in the evening helps as well.
Warm flannel. Okay. ~
If you get pain, redness, or blurred vision that doesn't clear when you blink, see your optician urgently.
I will. Thanks. ~
Take care. ~
